puremetal.options.renderScale.readout: Draws the world at %1$s×%2$s, then enlarges it to fill your screen (%3$s×%4$s).
puremetal.options.renderScale.readout.na: Draws the world at your full screen size (%1$s×%2$s). No upscaling.
puremetal.options.renderScale.tooltip: Fewer pixels = less GPU work = higher FPS. Menus and HUD stay sharp. Below 100%, MetalFX Temporal gives the steadiest image (less flicker on leaves and fences).
puremetal.options.autoRenderScale.toolti:
Automatically lowers Render Scale when your GPU can't keep up with your FPS target (Max FPS, or your display's refresh rate if unlimited), then raises it again when it can. Uses 100, 85, 70 and 60%. If a lower step doesn't make it faster, it goes back up and stops trying for a while.

Render Scale is set for you while this is on.
puremetal.options.upscaler.temporal.shad: Unavailable with shader packs; using Bilinear.
puremetal.options.upscaler.temporal.unsu: MetalFX couldn't start on this Mac; using Bilinear.
puremetal.options.upscaler.temporal.hook: Another mod changed rendering; using Bilinear.
puremetal.options.upscaler.note100: Upscalers only apply below 100% Render Scale.
puremetal.options.upscaler.tooltip:
Bilinear: fastest, softest.
MetalFX Spatial: sharper, costs a little FPS on M1/M2.
MetalFX Temporal: sharpest, may ghost on fast motion.
puremetal.options.metal4.tooltip:
Metal 3 (off): the default. Stable and currently the fastest option.
Metal 4 (on): Apple's newer GPU API. Experimental, usually slower for now and may have visual glitches. Needs macOS 26 and an M1 or newer.
Restart the game after changing this.
puremetal.options.metal4.unsupported: Requires macOS 26 or newer on Apple silicon. Metal 4 is unavailable on this system.
puremetal.options.note: Pure Metal already boosts FPS on its own. These settings are optional extras.
puremetal.options.inactive: Inactive: Pure Metal is not running.
puremetal.options.terrainLod.tooltip: Simplifies far terrain at Render Distance 16+. Nearby terrain stays full detail; distant solid blocks are drawn as bigger blocks, distant leaves are drawn solid, small plants are hidden far away and calm water surfaces are simplified. Glass is unchanged.
puremetal.options.terrainLodRatio.toolti: Share of Render Distance kept at full detail. Lower simplifies more terrain.
puremetal.options.generationFpsCap.toolt:
Loads new terrain faster in singleplayer.

The game draws frames and builds chunks on the same CPU. While chunks near you are still missing, FPS is limited to twice your refresh rate, so the CPU time saved goes to building chunks.

Normal FPS returns once they have loaded.
puremetal.options.batterySaver.tooltip:
Saves battery and keeps your Mac cooler by capping FPS at 60. If your Mac gets hot, drops to 30 FPS until it cools down.

A lower Max FPS you set is kept. Render Scale is not changed.
puremetal.options.hdrHighlights.tooltip:
Lets the sun, lava and glowing blocks shine brighter than normal white on Mac screens that support it.

Only very bright and fiery colors are boosted. Menus are never boosted, but the on-screen HUD can be if it is bright enough.

Needs a restart to take effect. May use a little more GPU. It does not brighten anything while Battery Saver is on.

Experimental.
puremetal.options.hdrHighlights.noScreen: Not active right now: this screen does not support HDR.
puremetal.options.smoothFramePacing.tool:
Makes motion look smoother when VSync is on.

Each frame is shown on the next display refresh, at an even rhythm, instead of the moment it is ready. This reduces small stutters when you turn the camera or move.

A frame that is already late is never held back.

Only works with VSync on.

Experimental.
puremetal.options.smoothFramePacing.vsyn: Has no effect right now: VSync is off.
puremetal.options.highRefreshBoost.vsync: Has no effect right now: VSync is on.
puremetal.options.highRefreshBoost.slowD: Has no effect right now: this display runs at %s Hz (needs 200 Hz or more).
puremetal.options.highRefreshBoost.force: Has no effect right now: a launch option decides this instead.
puremetal.options.highRefreshBoost.toolt:
For displays running at 200 Hz or faster with VSync off. Stops waiting for the next display refresh, so a finished frame can appear partway through one. This can show more frames per second and make motion smoother.

May cause screen tearing, mainly in fullscreen. Has no effect with VSync on or on slower displays.

Experimental.
